# Unequal positive normals can improve a nested simplex-chain cap

This is an exact obstruction to reducing the positive continuous normals
to coordinate normals or equal nonzero coefficients. It is not a depth
counterexample.

Let T={(x1,x2): x1,x2>=0, x1+x2<=1}, with area V=1/2. At integer
bases -1,0,1 place the fibers

    K_-=(1/2)T, K_0=(3/2)T, K_+=(3/4)T.

Their convex hull is a full-dimensional compact convex body with exactly
these three integer fibers: the endpoint midpoint radius is5/8<=3/2.
Take the actual middle centroid y=(0,1/2,1/2). For a in[1/2,1] and
beta in R consider the closed through-y cap

    a x1+(1-a)x2+beta z >= 1/2.                 (1)

The normalization a>=1/2 loses nothing within the class of nonnegative
continuous normals, because the entire source and point are invariant
under interchanging x1,x2. The following comparison concerns that class.

## 1. Exact triangular tail formula

For r>0, put t=1/2-beta z. The cap area in rT, divided by V, is

    r^2,                                      t<=0;
    r^2-t^2/[a(1-a)],                          0<=t<=(1-a)r;
    (ar-t)^2/[a(2a-1)],                        (1-a)r<=t<=ar;
    0,                                        t>=ar.         (2)

The two middle expressions follow by the intercept formula for the
triangle cut from the origin, and for the triangle retained at the
vertex(r,0), respectively. Their endpoints agree. For a=1 use the
limiting coordinate formula [r-t]^2 on0<=t<=r, clipped at0 andr^2.
For a=1/2 use r^2-4t^2 on0<=t<=r/2, clipped. Every cut line has
zero area, so this is also the exact closed-cap mass.

## 2. All coordinate-normal tilts

At a=1 the middle contribution is exactly V. The two other contributions,
divided by V, are the clipped squares of -beta and1/4+beta. On
[-1/4,0] no full-cap clipping occurs, and the total is

    1+beta^2+(1/4+beta)^2
      =33/32+2(beta+1/8)^2.                       (3)

For beta>=0 the left cap is zero and the right contribution is at
least1/16, even after it saturates at9/16. For beta<=-1/4 the right
cap is zero and the left contribution is at least1/16, even after
it saturates at1/4. Thus neither exterior region improves(3). Hence

    inf_beta mu(H_(1,beta))=(33/32)V,             (4)

attained at beta=-1/8. Coordinate interchange gives the same answer
for the other positive coordinate normal.

## 3. All equal-coefficient tilts

At a=1/2 the middle contribution alone is(5/4)V, independent of beta.
Both endpoint contributions vanish whenever -1/4<=beta<=1/8, since
their thresholds are at least their maximum a r. Therefore

    inf_beta mu(H_(1/2,beta))=(5/4)V.             (5)

## 4. One exact unequal-normal improvement

Choose a=6/7 and beta=-3/28. At the three bases the thresholds are
11/28,1/2,17/28. All three cuts are in the last proper-cap branch
of(2), with respective values of ar-t equal to1/28,11/14,1/28.
Their common denominator a(2a-1) is30/49. Consequently

    mu(H)/V=[(1/28)^2+(11/14)^2+(1/28)^2]/(30/49)
            =81/80
            <33/32<5/4.                         (6)

The first strict gap is exactly3/160. Thus optimizing every base tilt
within the coordinate and equal-coefficient directions cannot recover
the actual infimum even within positive continuous normals. No claim
is made that(6) is the globally minimal cap, or that all normals have
already been analyzed by this note.

The original source is explicitly OC-safe: its middle mass(9/4)V is
more than half the total(49/16)V. Ordinary planar Grünbaum at its
centroid gives absolute mass at least(4/9)(9/4)V=V in every containing
ambient halfspace, exceeding the OC target(2/9)(49/16)V=(49/72)V.
Vertical caps contain the whole middle fiber and also satisfy this bound.

The exact verifier certifies the support compatibility, all branch
conditions, rational cap values, and the algebraic restricted minima.
The all-parameter proofs of(4)-(5) are the explicit arguments above.
